title: Networked level reads nonsense
summary: Communication with the level transmitter is OK, yet the controller believes the nearly empty tank is full and never opens the valve.
objectives: Check a Modbus register map against the client configuration
starterProgram:
PROGRAM Main
VAR_INPUT
    StartPB : BOOL; (* Start button S1 (normally open). *)
    StopPB : BOOL; (* Stop button S2 (normally closed). *)
    LevelHighHigh : BOOL; (* Independent high-high switch at 90 % (TRUE when wet). *)
    LevelPermille : INT; (* Level from Modbus holding register 0 (40001), 0..1000 = 0..100 %. *)
    LevelPercent : REAL; (* Level from holding registers 1-2 (40002-40003), IEEE 754 float, high word first. *)
    LevelCommOK : BOOL; (* TRUE while the Modbus scan of the transmitter succeeds. *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    InletValve : BOOL; (* Inlet valve solenoid XV-101. *)
    DrainPump : BOOL; (* Drain pump P-102. *)
END_VAR
VAR
    Filling : BOOL;
END_VAR

Filling := (StartPB OR Filling) AND StopPB AND LevelCommOK AND NOT LevelHighHigh AND LevelPermille < 800;
InletValve := Filling;
DrainPump := FALSE;

END_PROGRAM
instructions: Compare LevelPermille with the real tank level.
Look at the raw registers in the Network tab.
Compare the transmitter's register map (holding register 0 = level in permille, registers 1-2 = level as float) with the configured start address.
Correct the configuration (Network tab, Advanced mode), download, then verify.
hints: Modbus addresses on the wire start at 0; documentation often writes 40001 for address 0.
A float32 high word interpreted as INT looks like a large number.

criteria.title: The valve closes at 80 %
criteria.onFail: InletValve stayed open after the networked level reached 80 %.

criteria.title: Filling requires valid communication
criteria.onFail: The valve was open while the transmitter was not communicating.

troubleshooting.symptom: The tank stays empty. The HMI shows a level above 100 % although the sight glass shows about 10 %. Communication status is OK.

diagnosisOptions.label: The Modbus read starts one register too late (address 1 instead of 0)
The float word order is wrong

debrief.rootCause: The Modbus client read started at register address 1 instead of 0, so the PLC received the high word of the level float instead of the permille level in holding register 0.
evidence: The communication status was OK, so addressing, unit identifier and the link were working.
LevelPermille showed a value far above 1000 while the sight glass showed about 10 %.
The raw registers showed the plausible level in register 0, one position before the configured start address.
The value did not follow the level linearly, which a pure scaling error would have done.
debrief.repair: Set the Modbus read start address to 0 in the network configuration and download the station.
debrief.reasoning: When communication is OK but the value is nonsense, compare the device's register map with the client configuration and look at the raw words. Off-by-one offsets are common because documentation often writes 40001 for wire address 0.
